newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker after rangebound session.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker after rangebound session.

text.p: COMEX copper settled slightly weaker in rangebound trading where most of the day's losses were pared just before the close.
A broker said the market rallied near the close due to shortcovering and said LME stocks Tuesday were expected to see a slight drop of somewhere between 500 and 1,000 tonnes.
December COMEX ended 0.25 cent lower at 86.60 cents per pound, traded narrowly between 86.70 and 85.90 cents. Spot September went out 0.75 cent weaker at 87.30 cents.

There was little fresh fundamental news in the market. However, negotiations between Ford Motor Co and the United Auto Workers Union resumed Monday and the company hoped a tentative agreement would be reached later in the day.
The auto sector is a major consumer of red metal and any prolonged strike would be felt on the physical market, which has remained buoyant in the United States.
Friday's CFTC Commitment of Traders report for week ended September 10 showed that commercials were heavily short in the market.
Commercials held 36,659 short positions and 22,568 long positions, while speculators held 8,704 long positions and 6,508 short positions.
